title: Why Keeping Up With Mattermost Upgrades Matters More Than Ever
summary: AI is accelerating vulnerability discovery and exploitation. The fix usually exists; the exposure comes from not applying it. Here is how to build an upgrade rhythm and stay on a supported Mattermost release.
body_markdown:
## **The world around your server has changed**


AI has changed the physics of cybersecurity. Frontier models are accelerating vulnerability discovery, and OpenAI describes the bottleneck as having moved from finding vulnerabilities to patching them ([OpenAI, Daybreak, June 2026](https://openai.com/index/daybreak-securing-the-world/) ).


The consequences show up in the data. J.P. Morgan’s July 2026 Eye on the Market reports that the average time between disclosure and first exploitation has fallen to about a day, and that in roughly 60% of breaches a patch was already available when the compromise happened ([Patchmageddon](https://cdn.jpmorganfunds.com/content/dam/jpm-am-aem/global/en/insights/eye-on-the-market/patchmageddon-amv.pdf) ). Put plainly: the fix usually exists, and the exposure comes from not applying it.


## **Why upgrades are the control that matters**


Mattermost holds the conversations, files and incident coordination that organizations depend on. When we fix a vulnerability, the fix ships in the supported releases. Details are published 30 days after the release is available so administrators have time to upgrade.


That protects servers that are current. It also means that once the details are public, attackers know about them too, and servers that haven’t upgraded stay exposed. A version that no longer receives fixes keeps every vulnerability found after its support ended.


## **Falling behind compounds**


Staying current is easier than catching up.


- **Bigger jumps are harder.** The tested path is ESR to ESR, and we don’t recommend skipping releases. Every release you skip adds changes to review and test at once.
- **Support windows are finite.** v10.11 ESR support ended on August 15, 2026. v11.7.4 ESR is supported until May 15, 2027.
- **Your plan stays smaller the more often you upgrade.** Small, regular upgrades are easier to test, easier to roll back and easier to schedule than rare, large ones.


## **Build an upgrade rhythm**


1. **Know your version.** Check System Console > About Mattermost.
2. **Choose a track.** Most organizations should follow the ESR track and plan an ESR-to-ESR upgrade before each support window ends. If you want new features sooner, follow the regular monthly releases.
3. **Put the dates on your calendar.** Plan your next upgrade at least a quarter before your version’s support ends.
4. **Test before production.** Keep a staging environment, back up your database and file storage, and review the release notes and the[important upgrade notes](https://docs.mattermost.com/administration-guide/upgrade/important-upgrade-notes) .
5. **Subscribe to security alerts.**[Get notified when a fix ships](https://mattermost.com/company/responsible-disclosure/#security-bulletin) .


## **If you are still on v10**


If you are still on v10, the recommended target is v11.7.4 ESR or later. Before upgrading, review the[important upgrade notes](https://docs.mattermost.com/administration-guide/upgrade/important-upgrade-notes) for every release in between to understand changes affecting your deployment. Be sure to allocate time to test plugins, integrations, and SSO configurations in staging, and keep in mind that v11 introduces updated free tier offerings, including a 10,000 message history limit for Mattermost Entry (see[Mattermost v11: changes in free offerings](https://forum.mattermost.com/t/mattermost-v11-changes-in-free-offerings/25126) for full details).


These are one-time costs you can plan for. Running unsupported software is a risk that grows every month it continues.


## **Getting the most from Mattermost: v12 launched October 2026**


Mattermost v12 is built for teams whose missions cannot stop: sovereign operations and AI, with stronger data controls, cross-domain coordination and AI-ready workflows, running in infrastructure you control, including classified and air-gapped environments.


- **Data-centric security.** Make classification visible across the user experience, and apply attribute-based policies that take identity, organizational structure and operating context into account.
- **Cross-domain coordination.** Connect collaboration across security domains through approved cross-domain infrastructure, with customer policies governing transfer.
- **Workflows and AI.** Bring alerts, people and repeatable processes into a shared operational workspace, with an open ecosystem for AI capabilities and a full audit trail and oversight throughout.
- **Built for demanding environments.** Self-manage on-premises, in private, sovereign and isolated clouds, and in networks with limited or no connection to the public internet.


Learn more:[Mattermost v12](https://mattermost.com/v12-ecosystem-that-comes-to-the-mission/) or[start a trial](https://mattermost.com/sign-up/) .

Read the[upgrade guide](https://docs.mattermost.com/administration-guide/upgrade/upgrading-mattermost-server.html) . If you are a paid customer and want help planning, contact us at[support.mattermost.com](https://support.mattermost.com/) .
